Rzeszow Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Rzeszów, Poland

Not demolished. This record shows a tension worth noting: it is categorized as 'demolished and overbuilt,' yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'no.' Rzeszów's Jewish community reached about 1,600 people (50 percent of the town) around 1700, and about 14,000 (35 percent) by the 1930s; one of its most eminent members, Rabbi Aaron Lewin, served in the Polish Parliament from 1922. This cemetery, established in the first half of the 16th century, incorporated a former city-fortification earthwork as burial ground from the 18th century onward. Between 1939 and 1942, the Germans completely destroyed the cemetery and leveled the earthwork, using the empty site as a deportation selection point; after 1945, Ghetto Victims Square was established there.
